seurat-grande-jatte: Seurat built this scene of Parisians relaxing on an island in the Seine from thousands of tiny dots of pure colour, a technique known as pointillism.
van-gogh-bedroom: Van Gogh painted his own bedroom in Arles in the south of France, using flat, bright colours and a tilted perspective. He made three versions; this is the one in Chicago.
van-gogh-self-portrait: Painted in Paris, this self-portrait shows Van Gogh experimenting with short, directional brushstrokes inspired by the pointillist painters around him.
monet-water-lilies: One of Monet’s many views of the water-lily pond in his garden at Giverny, where he painted the surface of the water and its reflections rather than the horizon.
monet-stacks-of-wheat: Monet painted the same haystacks near his home in Giverny again and again to capture how light and colour change with the season and the time of day.
caillebotte-paris-street: Caillebotte’s large view of a Paris intersection shows well-dressed pedestrians with umbrellas on wet cobblestones, a modern city seen with an almost photographic eye.
renoir-two-sisters: Renoir shows two young women on a terrace by the river, painted with soft, quick brushwork and a warm palette of reds, oranges and greens.
cassatt-childs-bath: Mary Cassatt composed this tender scene of a woman and a child from a high angle, influenced by the flat colours and bold design of Japanese woodblock prints.
toulouse-lautrec-moulin-rouge: Toulouse-Lautrec captured the nightlife of Montmartre with strong colours, cropped figures and a sharply cut-off composition that feels like a snapshot.
gauguin-day-of-the-god: Gauguin’s colourful scene of Tahitian life shows a carved idol above a pool of bathers, painted in flat, saturated colours rather than realistic shading.
cezanne-basket-of-apples: Cézanne tilted the table and shifted viewpoints so the bottle, basket and fruit seem to float in a space of their own, an approach that inspired later modern art.
hokusai-shower-below-the-summit: A woodblock print from Hokusai’s series of Mount Fuji views, showing a storm raging below the summit while the peak itself stays in clear sky.
vermeer-water-pitcher: A young woman opens a window and holds a water pitcher in a quiet room, lit by soft daylight, in one of Vermeer’s calm domestic scenes.
van-gogh-wheat-field-cypresses: Painted in 1889 in southern France, this view has swirling clouds and dark cypress trees rising from a golden wheat field.
sargent-madame-x: Sargent’s portrait of a Parisian socialite caused a scandal at the 1884 Salon, partly because of the daring neckline of the black dress.
rembrandt-aristotle-homer: The philosopher Aristotle rests a hand on a bust of the poet Homer in a portrait known for its rich golden light and deep, dark background.
hokusai-great-wave: The best-known Japanese woodblock print: a towering wave about to crash over fishing boats, with Mount Fuji small in the distance.
degas-dance-class: Degas shows young ballet students waiting and stretching in a rehearsal room while their teacher looks on, a moment caught between the steps.
